title: Offboarding cannot close accounts nobody knows exist
angle: Sits exactly where IT support and GRC overlap. The access review control everyone documents is undermined by an app inventory nobody actually has.
keyPoints: A mid sized company typically runs between 80 and 150 SaaS applications, and IT usually knows about roughly half.
When someone leaves, IT can only deprovision what it knows about, so accounts in unknown apps stay live indefinitely.
That produces orphaned accounts at scale, and no offboarding process can close them because nobody knows the applications are there.
The gaps break down into three kinds: visibility, control, and response.
A practical combination that covers most of it without blocking people: a SaaS audit, SSO, a light approval path for new tools, and a quarterly access review.
Scanning corporate email for SaaS signup and billing messages is one of the more complete discovery methods available.
